agentPrompt.generic:
When you produce a plan, spec or report longer than ~50 lines, write it to a .md file and open it for the user in Mark.
Mark renders rich Markdown. Use the right tool for each part instead of plain prose:
- Diagrams — ```mermaid fences; pick the type that fits: flowchart (processes, decisions), sequenceDiagram (who calls whom), classDiagram, stateDiagram-v2 (lifecycles), erDiagram (data models), gantt (schedules), timeline (history, milestones), gitGraph (branches), mindmap (idea maps), journey (user journeys), quadrantChart (priorities), pie, xychart-beta (bar/line charts), sankey-beta (flows of quantities), block-beta, packet-beta, kanban, architecture-beta, radar-beta, treemap-beta, requirementDiagram, C4Context. Prefer a diagram to a paragraph describing a structure.
- Charts from data — ```vega-lite with a JSON spec; quick flowcharts — ```flowchart (flowchart.js); quick sequences — ```sequence.
- Tables (with column alignment) for comparisons, options and matrices.
- Callouts for what must not be missed: > [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], [!CAUTION]; also info, todo, success, question, failure, danger, bug, example, quote, abstract. Put a title after the tag; add - or + to make it foldable.
- Task lists (- [ ] / - [x]) for next steps and checklists.
- Math — $…$ inline and $$…$$ blocks (KaTeX).
- Code — fenced blocks with a language for highlighting.
- Footnotes ([^1]) for sources and asides; YAML front matter for metadata; emoji :shortcodes:; links and images.

Keep it scannable: short sections with headings, one idea per paragraph.
When the file changed after you wrote it, re-read it: the user's edits are your next instruction.

theme.title: Diagrams follow the theme
theme.text: Switch light ↔ dark and diagrams recolor instantly, without re-rendering.

lighter.title: A much lighter Mark
lighter.text: Diagram code: one 0.26 MB part (compressed) instead of 44 parts totalling 2.6 MB.

engine.title: A new diagram engine
engine.text: Diagrams render with Pele — faster and far lighter. The look has changed.

types.title: New diagram types
types.text: Venn, treemap, agentflow, radar, swimlane, usecase and more in mermaid blocks.

columns.title: Column widths stay put
columns.text: Drag a column border once and the width stays for that file. The Markdown is untouched.

session.title: Picks up where you left off
session.text: Mark reopens your folder and tabs on launch. Turn it off in Settings › General.

updates.title: Updates come to you
updates.text: Mark checks for a new version once a day: update now, later, or skip it.

tables.title: Wide tables at full width
tables.text: A table wider than the page opens at full width; Fit to page is kept per table.

notes.title: Only your notes
notes.text: Folders show Markdown files only, with Recent and Pinned on top.

diagrams.title: Diagrams that match the theme
diagrams.text: Mermaid, charts and math take the theme's colours; open any of them full screen.

home.title: A home screen
home.text: Recent files and folders, the Guide, and one click to connect your agent.

look.title: A calmer, native-looking Mark
look.text: New Paper, Ink, Docs and macOS themes, a slim title bar and an outline beside the page.

export.title: Diagrams as pictures
export.text: Copy any diagram or chart as an image, or save it as PNG or SVG.

print.title: Print and PDF, each direct
print.text: Print goes straight to the system panel; Export to PDF saves the file without it.

images.title: Copy images back out
images.text: Copy a picture that is already in the document back to the clipboard.

look.title: A look for each diagram
look.text: Auto, the author's palette, light or dark — chosen per diagram and saved with it.

wideTables.title: Wide tables, under control
wideTables.text: Fit and Full width stay put; panning cues show where more columns wait.

compare.title: Compare with when opened
compare.text: ⌘D compares a note with the version Mark opened, even outside a Git repository.

tableImages.title: Tables as pictures
tableImages.text: Copy a table as an image, or save a PNG from the full-screen viewer.

shortcuts.title: Editing shortcuts restored
shortcuts.text: ⇧⌘D duplicates a paragraph; ⌘1–6 turns it into an H1–H6 heading.

session.title: Sessions, honestly
session.text: Mark restores tabs and folder at launch; ⇧⌘T reopens a closed one, counted on the row.

htmlExport.title: Self-contained HTML
htmlExport.text: Export as HTML now embeds local images — one .html file travels anywhere on its own.

shortcuts.title: ⇧⌘P opens the palette
shortcuts.text: The command palette has its Mac shortcut back, and table exports keep every real cell.

windowsBar.title: Native Windows title bar
windowsBar.text: Windows and Linux get true system caption buttons and the theme toggle inside the bar.

folders.title: ⇧⌘O adds another folder
folders.text: Work in several folders at once; Replace Workspace… swaps them safely.

cloud.title: Cloud folders open natively
cloud.text: iCloud Drive and OneDrive folders work as roots; online-only files say so once.

search.title: Search that keeps up
search.text: Folder search labels each hit with its folder and keeps every result as you type.

quit.title: ⌘Q asks before quitting
quit.text: Unsaved edits get Save & Quit or Don’t Save — nothing disappears silently anymore.

pdfFix.title: PDF export fixed
pdfFix.text: Export to PDF no longer crashes the app and writes your document to disk.
